clue.text: Ritual dancer in confusion drives around, given second chance

parts.note: a head that is whirling is in confusion

indicators.note: letters sent around are moved about and land in a new order
second points to the letter in position two of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone muddled by driving round and round is grateful for another go.
explanation.walkthrough: WHIRLING, meaning in a whirl or confused, comes first, then DRIVES rearranged plus the H from chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling dervish is a Sufi devotee who spins as a form of religious devotion and meditation.

clue.text: Operating more than half of what a stable government needs

parts.note: a machine that is operating is working
a majority is more than half of a group

explanation.surface: A description of how much a functioning government must command to stay steady.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay half reads almost like a second definition: operating gives the first word, more than half the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A working majority is a parliamentary margin large enough for a ruling party to pass its business reliably.

clue.text: Is girl one's offspring?

explanation.surface: A parent asking whether a certain young woman is their child.
explanation.walkthrough: Read one's as one is: IS plus SUE is offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal, chiefly legal word for a person's children or descendants.

clue.text: The French star climbing round one with ropes

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word reads upward, from bottom to top
going round something means wrapping it, so one word is placed outside another

explanation.surface: A French celebrity scaling a wall, roped up as climbers are.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, climbing reverses upward; the inserted one is the Roman numeral, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Lariats are lassos, long ropes with running nooses used by cowboys to catch cattle and horses.

clue.text: Sort of vain, yet displaying innocence

indicators.note: a sort of something is a version of it, so these letters come out in a different form

explanation.surface: Someone a little conceited who nonetheless comes across as innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is a lack of worldly experience and judgement, which is what innocence means here.

clue.text: Pitch tent in river for relaxation?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

explanation.surface: A camper setting up a tent in the water, presumably for a restful break.
explanation.walkthrough: The river Dee is a crossword staple; TENT goes between its first and second letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Detente is a relaxation of tension between countries, especially the easing of Cold War hostility.

clue.text: Get real about endless fuss caused by denial

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the next
without an end means the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Telling someone to be realistic about a pointless fuss that came from being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get real' reads as a slangy command, but only the word real is used; it wraps the shortened fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a denial of a request, a saying no to something asked for.

clue.text: Disguised by putting icing onto mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: Covering up a botched bake by spreading icing over it.
explanation.walkthrough: Mess reads as a noun for a ruined cake, but it is the anagram signal on icing onto.
explanation.definitionFit: Incognito describes someone concealing their true identity, travelling under an assumed name or in disguise.

clue.text: How content is a lad on the beach

definitions.text: How content is a lad on the beach

parts.words: How content is a lad on the beach
parts.note: surface reading: asking how happy a boy enjoying the seaside is; setter's reading: a boy on the sand names the old simile for being very contented

explanation.walkthrough: The British simile compares a contented person to a sandboy, originally a hawker of sand; the clue reads it literally as a boy on the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means extremely pleased and contented, a stock comparison for carefree happiness.

clue.text: Hold train in idleness

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first word is placed within the next

parts.note: rest is a state of idleness

explanation.surface: A train kept waiting, sitting idle at the platform.
explanation.walkthrough: Hold looks like a verb but defines a noun here: restraint, as in holding back.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is the act of holding back or keeping someone under control, a noun sense of hold.

clue.text: Initially, fittest agile chap under par gets a sporting trophy

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word in the run that follows

parts.note: the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A sprightly player who isn't feeling his best still lifts the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA Cup is English football's knockout competition, run by the Football Association.
explanation.definitionFit: The FA Cup is the trophy for the oldest national football competition, contested by English clubs each season.

clue.text: Tie knotted at speed? Say again!

indicators.note: something knotted is twisted out of shape, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tying a necktie in a hurry, asked to repeat something.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat or restate, as in performing or saying something once more.

clue.text: Goes wild in refusal to provide a posy

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the scrambled letters go within the next word

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so the letters before it scatter

explanation.surface: Someone reacts furiously when refused a little bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of fragrant flowers, the same thing as a posy.

clue.text: Nip the little one?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: A question about pinching a toddler.
explanation.walkthrough: Nip looks like a verb, to pinch, but it is the noun for a small measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word means both a small dram of whisky or similar and a very young child.

clue.text: Disagree with profit, for instance

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example

explanation.surface: Someone who objects to making money, as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or deny, speaking against what someone else asserts.

clue.text: Without planning, I'm on time — you, too, by the sound of it!

indicators.note: judging by sound means the words are spoken and heard, not read

parts.note: being on time is being prompt, and you is added

explanation.surface: Someone noting that both of you arrived punctually, as if by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Impromptu means done on the spur of the moment, without rehearsal or preparation.

clue.text: Dread a weird experience, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: first letters of the three words; that the answer also runs through 'a weird' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Fear felt first of all as a strange experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential fear or dread inspired by something vast, powerful or uncanny.

clue.text: Cakes that don't last long in City dens!

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London
a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: Pastries are snapped up quickly in the hideaways of city workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclairs are cream-filled pastries, and the playful extension notes they are eaten as soon as they appear.

clue.text: Tea and interminable talk

indicators.note: having no end means the last letter of the next word is cut

explanation.surface: Tea served with endless gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is an informal British word for tea, also spelt char.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha comes from the Chinese word for the drink and is slang for a cup of tea.

clue.text: Clothes worn by a very quiet earl, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several versions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: pianissimo, the musical direction for very quiet

explanation.surface: Garments put on by a reserved nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for clothing, the garments a person wears.

clue.text: The effects of the right lutes playing, up to a point

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: instruments playing make music, and here the letters play into a new order

explanation.surface: Describing what happens when a few early instruments are played reasonably well.
explanation.walkthrough: Up to a point sounds like a qualifier meaning partly; here it adds a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Results are the consequences or outcomes that follow from something, its effects.

clue.text: Mary's pet joins girl for a dance

parts.note: Mary had a little lamb, in the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: Mary's pet animal partners a girl on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast, sensual Brazilian couples dance popular in the late 1980s.

clue.text: Works out marine measurements

definitions.meaning: first meaning: understands, gets to the bottom of
second meaning: units of six feet used for sea depth

explanation.surface: Someone calculating depths at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom is to comprehend a puzzle, and a fathom is the nautical unit of six feet for depth.

clue.text: Payment for travel as tour begins in the Orient

parts.note: a fare is the price of a journey

indicators.note: where something begins is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

explanation.surface: Buying tickets as an Eastern holiday gets under way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Far East is the eastern part of Asia, the region long called the Orient in Western usage.

clue.text: Imitate a plane's rising

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mimic someone, as a verb phrase
second meaning: an aircraft leaving the ground

explanation.surface: An impressionist copying an aircraft's climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off someone is to mimic them, and an aircraft's takeoff is its departure from the runway.

clue.text: Muslim chief's not in again

indicators.note: not having something means it is taken away from the word that follows

explanation.surface: A Muslim leader is out of the office once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the word in off the end of again.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga is a commander or chief official in the Ottoman Empire and other Muslim countries.

clue.text: Work on very large amount for an animal

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Putting in a great deal of effort on behalf of a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: OS for outsize appears on clothing labels.
explanation.definitionFit: An opossum is an American marsupial, the possum, so it is one example of an animal.

clue.text: Brought together by roue's racket?

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute man, a rake
a din is a racket, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A debauched man's noisy carousing gathering people up.
explanation.definitionFit: Raked in means gathered together in quantity, as of money or leaves collected with a rake.

clue.text: Five hundred, healthy and live

parts.note: the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Reaching five hundred, in good health and still alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside or make one's home somewhere, a sense of live as a verb.

clue.text: Thrust the little devil onto the Spanish

parts.note: an imp is a small devil

explanation.surface: Someone shoving a mischievous child towards a Spaniard.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push forward, to propel something with force.

clue.text: Depressed when the tide's out?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: feeling down, low in spirits
setter's reading: the sea at its lowest point of the cycle

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for being in a poor state is read literally as the moment of lowest tide.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person or thing in a weak or dispirited condition, at a nadir.

clue.text: Misplaced fury at sly, foul hit; no time to finish a formal letter

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong positions, so these letters are shuffled
no means without, so the following item is removed from the fodder

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A boxing complaint about a sneaky low blow, wrapped up in correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the T from hit, then rearrange all the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Yours faithfully is the conventional British sign-off closing a formal letter addressed to an unnamed recipient.
